headline.title: This week at a glance
headline.summary: The Ebola Bundibugyo PHEIC enters a stabilisation-and-countermeasures phase: 282 confirmed cases and 42 confirmed deaths, with candidate therapeutics now prioritised for emergency trials. US measles has reached 1,983 cases — elimination status formally at risk. H5N1 avian influenza records a third unknown-exposure case among US humans, heightening pandemic-preparedness concern.
headline.takeaway: The Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in DRC and Uganda enters a critical transition from emergency response to countermeasure deployment. As of 31 May, DRC reports 282 confirmed cases across 17 health zones in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, plus 220 suspected cases under investigation, with 42 confirmed deaths. Five people have now recovered — including four nurses — a first positive signal. WHO and Africa CDC have prioritised three candidate therapeutics for emergency-use trials: the monoclonal antibodies MBP 134 and maftivimab, and the antiviral remdesivir. The oral antiviral obeldesivir is being prioritised for post-exposure prophylaxis, and two candidate BVD vaccines have been identified for clinical evaluation. Cross-border risk remains elevated: Uganda has 9 confirmed cases and 1 death, all linked to DRC travel. US measles surpassed 1,983 confirmed cases as of 28 May — across 40 US jurisdictions, 30 active outbreaks — putting elimination status formally at risk for the first time since 2000. H5N1 avian influenza has now recorded 3 US human cases with unknown animal-exposure source out of 71 total, raising concern about gaps in surveillance and possible cryptic spread.

pathogens.name: Ebola Bundibugyo
pathogens.scientific_name: Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BVD) — DRC & Uganda PHEIC · countermeasure trials underway
pathogens.location: DRC: Ituri (264 confirmed), North Kivu (15), South Kivu (3) · Uganda: 9 confirmed, 1 death
pathogens.why: The outbreak has shifted from explosive growth into a high-intensity stabilisation phase. As of 31 May 2026, DRC reports 282 confirmed cases in 17 health zones across Ituri (264), North Kivu (15) and South Kivu (3), plus 220 suspected cases under investigation. Uganda has 9 confirmed cases and 1 death. Total confirmed deaths stand at 42. Critically, 5 people have recovered — including 4 nurses — a first clear evidence that survival with supportive care is achievable. WHO and Africa CDC R&D Blueprint have shortlisted candidate countermeasures for emergency-use clinical trials: monoclonal antibodies MBP 134 and maftivimab, remdesivir (IV/oral), obeldesivir (oral; targeted for post-exposure prophylaxis), and two BVD vaccine candidates. The Title 42 entry restriction (DRC, Uganda, South Sudan) remains in force. Nosocomial transmission in health-care settings continues to be a key driver; IPC training and PPE supply remain critical gaps.
policy_bullets: Accelerate WHO/Africa CDC R&D Blueprint emergency-use clinical-trial protocols for MBP 134, maftivimab and remdesivir in DRC and Uganda; coordinate regulatory fast-track pathways so enrolment can begin within days, not weeks.

Operationalise obeldesivir post-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk healthcare contacts; data from the five confirmed recoveries should inform supportive-care protocols for treatment centres in Bunia, Mongbwalu and Kampala.

Maintain cross-border exit screening between DRC, Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan, CAR and Kenya; sustain Title 42 screening at US ports of entry while avoiding broad travel-restriction language that depresses voluntary healthcare-seeking.

Prioritise IPC surge: 17 affected health zones, several with ongoing nosocomial amplification; emergency PPE pre-positioning and rapid IPC training for frontline health workers must be resourced separately from case-isolation funding.

pathogens.name: Measles (USA)
pathogens.scientific_name: Measles morbillivirus — largest US outbreak since 2019; elimination status formally at risk
pathogens.location: 40 US jurisdictions · 30 active outbreaks · Utah, Texas, Ohio, California leading

stats.label: Confirmed US cases in 2026 (as of 28 May)

pathogens.why: With 1,983 confirmed cases across 40 US jurisdictions as of 28 May 2026, the US is tracking closely to its full-year 2025 total of 2,288 — with seven months of 2026 remaining. Thirty new outbreaks have been identified in 2026 alone (93% of cases are outbreak-associated), and epidemiologists have publicly flagged that elimination status — held since 2000 — is formally at risk. Nine of the 1,983 cases are international visitors, confirming ongoing importation risk. The core driver is declining MMR vaccination coverage in select communities and states. A spike in post-outbreak vaccination rates has been documented, but structural coverage gaps in unvaccinated communities remain.
policy_bullets: Immediately assess MMR vaccination coverage at county level in all 40 affected jurisdictions and identify sub-80% coverage pockets — those are the outbreak accelerants that must be addressed with targeted catch-up campaigns.

Activate state emergency vaccination authority where outbreaks are active: school-exemption review, mobile vaccination teams, and community partnership with faith and school networks in hesitant communities.

Coordinate with CDC, APHA and ASTHO to formally communicate the elimination-status risk threshold — policymakers need to understand that the US could lose WHO measles-elimination certification if current trends continue.
Fund real-time outbreak surveillance: 93% outbreak-association rate means most cases are preventable with faster ring-vaccination response at outbreak detection.

details.Full-year 2025 total: 2,288 — 2026 on pace to exceed at current trajectory
details.Elimination status: Formally at risk — WHO certification requires sustained interruption of endemic transmission
details.Transmission: Airborne; one of the most transmissible human pathogens known
details.Clinical: Fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, rash; complications include pneumonia, encephalitis, SSPE
details.Key driver: Declining MMR coverage in select US communities; school exemptions; vaccine hesitancy

pathogens.name: H5N1 Avian Influenza
pathogens.scientific_name: Influenza A(H5N1) — 71 US human cases; 3 unknown-exposure; novel H5N5 human case
pathogens.location: USA (dairy cows, poultry workers) · Bangladesh (fatal paediatric case) · global wild-bird reservoir

stats.label: US human cases since 2024 (as of 27 May)

pathogens.why: The US multistate H5N1 outbreak in dairy cows and poultry continues to generate sporadic human cases. As of 27 May 2026, 71 US human infections have been confirmed since 2024, with 2 deaths. The most concerning signal this week: 3 of those 71 cases have no identified animal-exposure source — raising the possibility of missed exposures, environmental exposure, or limited undetected human-to-human transmission. No sustained H2H spread has been documented. Globally, WHO tracked 13 avian and swine influenza cases in humans in Q1 2026, including a fatal H5N1 case in a child in Bangladesh. A NEJM report documents the first confirmed human infection with H5N5 — a novel variant requiring close monitoring. Scientists have publicly warned that H5N1 could spark a human pandemic in 2026.
policy_bullets: Urgently investigate all 3 unknown-exposure US H5N1 cases with full environmental and contact-tracing workups; any evidence of human-to-human transmission must trigger immediate escalation to pandemic preparedness activation.
Strengthen surveillance in dairy-farm workers: serological screening beyond symptomatic testing — asymptomatic H5N1 cases are likely being missed given the unknown-exposure detections.

Accelerate H5N1 pandemic vaccine candidate production and pre-positioning; WHO and HHS should review current CVV stock against circulating H5 clade 2.3.4.4b strains and update if antigenic drift is detected.
Monitor H5N5 (novel variant, first human case NEJM 2026) — ensure national reference labs can distinguish H5 subtypes; add to WHO global surveillance net.

details.US states affected: California, Colorado, Iowa, Louisiana, Michigan, Missouri, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Texas, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming
details.Global Q1 2026: 13 avian/swine influenza cases in humans (WHO); includes fatal H5N1 in child, Bangladesh
details.H2H transmission: None sustained as of reporting date
details.Risk assessment (CDC): Low for general US public; moderate for workers with animal exposure
details.Pathogen: Influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b — highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI)
details.Reservoir: Wild birds (global); US dairy cows (novel mammalian reservoir, 2024–)
details.Clinical: Pneumonia, ARDS, multi-organ failure; historical CFR ~60% globally (milder in US dairy-worker cases)
details.Vaccines: No licensed H5N1 vaccine for general public; candidates in US strategic stockpile
details.Antivirals: Oseltamivir effective if started early; US SNS stockpile maintained
